source.title: Decomposing and Editing Predictions by Modeling Model Computation
source.authors: Harshay Shah; Andrew Ilyas; A. Ma̧dry

record.file_problem: None; the full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites the IOI circuit work but does not test IOI behavior or the circuit. Its GPT-2 experiment concerns next-token prediction on TinyStories.
record.gate_note: The GPT-2 results concern how well COAR estimates effects of component ablations on next-token prediction margins, not whether IOI is carried by the claimed circuit. The paper also reports other model and editing results, but they do not test the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper (COAR) cites the IOI work only as a source of zero-ablation practice and as an example of localization. Its GPT-2 experiment predicts weight-vector ablation effects on TinyStories next-token margins. It never runs the IOI task, never identifies attention-head classes and never evaluates any IOI circuit, so its results bear on no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that COAR yields predictive component attributions across vision and language models, GPT-2 on TinyStories included, and that these attributions enable ablation-based model editing. They draw no conclusion about the IOI circuit.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses regression-based component attribution for ablations of weight-vector components and evaluates counterfactual prediction correlations. It does not identify or test the IOI attention-head circuit.
record.method_sensitivity: For GPT-2 on TinyStories, the reported average correlation varies with evaluation ablation fraction: 0.83 at 5%, 0.85 at 2.5%, and 0.89 at 1%.

fits_no_version.finding: For GPT-2 on TinyStories, linear COAR attributions over 64,512 weight vectors predict zero-ablation effects on average correct-class margin. Average correlations are 0.83, 0.85 and 0.89 at 5%, 2.5% and 1% evaluation ablation fractions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear component attributions fit by regression predict the effects of random weight-vector ablations on GPT-2 next-token margins.

record.problems: The relevant GPT-2 result is for TinyStories next-token prediction rather than IOI; it reports correlation of attribution estimates with ablation counterfactuals, not IOI performance or circuit roles. Uncertainty estimates are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Other reported experiments and results are omitted because they do not concern the IOI circuit or GPT-2 IOI behavior.

record.verdict_notes: The IOI paper [WVC+22] is cited only to justify zero-ablation as a common choice and in related work on circuits. Remark 2 notes that ablation is not removal and shifts activations off-distribution, but this is a general methodological remark, not an IOI result. The rows report the study's own method performance and could be dropped.
